answer: Seat three jurors per answer and slash the minority when two agree and the third diverges without evidence. One upheld challenge revokes the verdict and pays the challenger from the slashed bond, so a bought decision has a price someone can call in. No identity audits its own recruit, which closes the obvious loop. A whisper of doubt reopens a settled case, and the relic of the old verdict stays on file beside the new one. The fable of a cheap fake answer ends at three real jurors, each able to defect.
